name: Local Coefficient-Row Extension Identities
statement: For fixed positive normalized rows $R$ at a concept $c$, the local separator inequalities are feasible exactly when those on the positive-front residual family $\rho_c(R)$ are feasible. Moreover, for every $H\subseteq R$, coefficient restriction satisfies $\operatorname{pr}_H\mathcal F_c(R)=\mathcal F_c(H)$. Rational prescribed rows and witnesses extend rationally.
proof: Reverse each positive-front deletion by raising its favorable private witness coordinate, which restores all deleted rows without changing surviving inequalities. For a new arbitrary row, choose one disagreement coordinate, make its raw coefficient dominate the weighted agreement sum, and normalize; rows extend independently.
